{{Use dmy dates|date=December 2021}}
'''Gerd Jürgens''' (also spelt Juergens) (born 1949) is a plant developmental biologist and emeritus Director of the Cell Biology Department at the Max Planck Institute for Developmental Biology<ref name="Max-Planck-Gesellschaft 2021">{{cite web | title=Jürgens, Gerd | website=Max-Planck-Gesellschaft | date=21 October 2021 | url=https://www.mpg.de/463999/entwicklungsbiologie-juergens | language=de | access-date=16 December 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.eb.tuebingen.mpg.de/emeriti/cell-biology/|title=Cell Biology|website=www.eb.tuebingen.mpg.de|accessdate=16 December 2021}}</ref> and Head of the Center for Plant Molecular Biology (ZMBP) at the [[University of Tübingen|Eberhard-Karls Universität Tübingen]]. He has published extensively in leading journals, including eight papers in the journal ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' as well as various articles in the journals ''[[Cell (journal)|Cell]]'', ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'', ''[[Journal of Cell Biology]]'' and ''[[The Plant Journal]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.mnf.uni-tuebingen.de/fachbereiche/zentren/zmbp/developmental-genetics/juergens/publications.html |title=Zentrum für Molekularbiologie der Pflanzen - Pub |access-date=26 December 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110719111523/http://www.mnf.uni-tuebingen.de/fachbereiche/zentren/zmbp/developmental-genetics/juergens/publications.html |archive-date=19 July 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Research==
During his postdoctoral years in the 1980s he worked with [[Nobel Prize]] winners [[Christiane Nüsslein-Volhard]] and [[Eric Wieschaus]] at the [[European Molecular Biology Laboratory]] (EMBL) in Heidelberg on the topic of ''[[Drosophila melanogaster]]'' embryogenesis.<ref name="Laureate. 1942">{{cite web | title=The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 1995 | website=NobelPrize.org | date=20 October 1942 | url=https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/1995/nusslein-volhard/biographical/ | access-date=16 December 2021}}</ref>
At the age of 37 he made the switch from animal to plant research and became one of the first researchers to work on what was later to become the [[model organism|model plant organism]]: ''[[Arabidopsis thaliana]]''.
He was responsible for pioneering research in the genetic dissection of [[plant embryogenesis]]. Using the genetically-tractable plant ''[[Arabidopsis thaliana]]'' he conducted the first [[forward genetics|forward genetic]] screen (using mutagenesis with 0.3% [[ethyl methane sulfonate]] (EMS)) looking for embryonic defects.<ref name="Mayer Ruiz Berleth Miséra 1991 pp. 402–407">{{cite journal | last1=Mayer | first1=Ulrike | last2=Ruiz | first2=Ramón A. Torres | last3=Berleth | first3=Thomas | last4=Miséra | first4=Simon | last5=Jürgens | first5=Gerd | title=Mutations affecting body organization in the Arabidopsis embryo | journal=Nature | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=353 | issue=6343 | year=1991 | issn=0028-0836 | doi=10.1038/353402a0 | pages=402–407| bibcode=1991Natur.353..402M | s2cid=4282406 }}</ref>
His laboratory discovered and characterized the protein KNOLLE, which is required for [[cytokinesis]] and was the first protein known to exclusively target the [[cell plate]] in plant cells.<ref name="Lukowitz Mayer Jürgens 1996 pp. 61–71">{{cite journal | last1=Lukowitz | first1=Wolfgang | last2=Mayer | first2=Ulrike | last3=Jürgens | first3=Gerd | title=Cytokinesis in the Arabidopsis Embryo Involves the Syntaxin-Related KNOLLE Gene Product | journal=Cell | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=84 | issue=1 | year=1996 | issn=0092-8674 | doi=10.1016/s0092-8674(00)80993-9 | pages=61–71| pmid=8548827 | s2cid=6493229 | doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name="Lauber Waizenegger Steinmann Schwarz pp. 1485–1493">{{cite journal | last1=Lauber | first1=Martina H. | last2=Waizenegger | first2=Irene | last3=Steinmann | first3=Thomas | last4=Schwarz | first4=Heinz | last5=Mayer | first5=Ulrike | last6=Hwang | first6=Inwhan | last7=Lukowitz | first7=Wolfgang | last8=Jürgens | first8=Gerd | title=The Arabidopsis KNOLLE Protein Is a Cytokinesis-specific Syntaxin | journal=Journal of Cell Biology | publisher=Rockefeller University Press | volume=139 | issue=6 | date=15 December 1997 | issn=0021-9525 | doi=10.1083/jcb.139.6.1485 | pages=1485–1493| pmid=9396754 | pmc=2132613 }}</ref>
Jürgens also worked extensively on the [[ADP ribosylation factor|ARF]]-[[Guanine nucleotide exchange factor|GEF]] GNOM.<ref name="Geldner Anders Wolters Keicher 2003 pp. 219–230">{{cite journal |last1=Geldner |first1=Niko |author-link=Niko Geldner |last2=Anders |first2=Nadine |last3=Wolters |first3=Hanno |last4=Keicher |first4=Jutta |last5=Kornberger |first5=Wolfgang |last6=Muller |first6=Philippe |last7=Delbarre |first7=Alain |last8=Ueda |first8=Takashi |last9=Nakano |first9=Akihiko |last10=Jürgens |first10=Gerd |year=2003 |title=The Arabidopsis GNOM ARF-GEF Mediates Endosomal Recycling, Auxin Transport, and Auxin-Dependent Plant Growth |journal=Cell |publisher=Elsevier BV |volume=112 |issue=2 |pages=219–230 |doi=10.1016/s0092-8674(03)00003-5 |issn=0092-8674 |pmid=12553910 |s2cid=9199922|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name="Anders Nielsen Keicher Stierhof pp. 142–151">{{cite journal | last1=Anders | first1=Nadine | last2=Nielsen | first2=Michael | last3=Keicher | first3=Jutta | last4=Stierhof | first4=York-Dieter | last5=Furutani | first5=Masahiko | last6=Tasaka | first6=Masao | last7=Skriver | first7=Karen | last8=Jürgens | first8=Gerd | title=Membrane Association of theArabidopsisARF Exchange Factor GNOM Involves Interaction of Conserved Domains | journal=The Plant Cell | publisher=Oxford University Press (OUP) | volume=20 | issue=1 | date=1 January 2008 | issn=1532-298X | doi=10.1105/tpc.107.056515 | pages=142–151| pmid=18203920 | pmc=2254928 | s2cid=11144074 }}</ref> Both ''knolle'' and ''gnom'' were first discovered in his embryonic mutant [[genetic screen|screens]].<ref name="Mayer Ruiz Berleth Miséra 1991 pp. 402–407"/>

== Prizes and awards ==
Jürgens won the [[Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize]] (the highest research award in Germany) in 1995.
